title: constrained decoding backends: CFG grammar + regex constraints + tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Asha Patel
description: Add and stabilize constrained decoding backends for structured output by implementing a CFG/grammar backend, improving regex-based constraints, and fixing tokenizer edgecases that caused invalid structured outputs. Motivation: multiple customers and internal evals showed brittle structured output behavior when using complex grammars or regex constraints, and tokenization inconsistencies produced invalid JSON/XML tokens on streaming endpoints. This PR introduces a new cfg_backend with a compact runtime representation of grammar rules and streaming-safe production handling, upgrades the existing regex backend to support lookahead/lookbehind-safe matches and lazy anchors compatible with subtokenization, and fixes tokenizer boundary cases that caused escape sequences and punctuation to split invalidly. Implementation highlights: 1) cfg backend: new parser/bytecode emitter that compiles user-supplied grammars into a stack-machine for streaming decoding; supports prioritized rules and partial-production buffering so streaming tokens do not violate intermediate constraints; uses the existing decoding trait so it can be swapped into runtime routing policies. 2) regex backend: switched matching engine to a DFA-fallback with a bounded backtracking cap and token-aligned matching to avoid mismatches across subtokens; added canonicalization layer to transform common user regexes into token-aware variants. 3) tokenizer fixes: canonicalized token boundaries for common punctuation and escape characters, added a normalization pass that ensures tokens starting/ending mid-unicode-grapheme are handled deterministically, and introduced tokenizer-aware prefix/suffix anchors used by both backends. 4) Compatibility: updated openai compatibility layer to expose structured_output.constraint_type and constraint_payload fields and to return clear decode_failure diagnostics on invalid outputs. 5) Tests: comprehensive unit + integration suite added: grammar roundtrip tests, fuzzed regex edgecases, tokenizer regression fixtures (including historical failing prompts from ENG-3421), and an end-to-end streaming conformance test against the OpenAI-compatible API surface. 6) Performance: microbenchmarks show ~5-8% decode overhead on heavy constraint sets vs previous uninstrumented regex approach, and the cfg backend has better determinism for large grammars under batching. Rollout plan: start with opt-in feature flag for dedicated and hosted beta customers, monitor structured-output error rate and decode latency dashboards, then flip on by default for new API users after two weeks of stable metrics. Backwards compatibility: existing unconstrained decoding unchanged; added clear error messages for older clients using the previous constraint payload shape. See release notes below for user-facing changes.

release_notes: Added new CFG/grammar constrained-decoding backend and improved regex constraints with tokenizer-aware matching. Fixed tokenizer edgecases that caused invalid structured outputs on streaming endpoints. Exposed structured_output.constraint_type and diagnostics in OpenAI compatibility layer. Opt-in feature flag for rollout. Non-breaking for existing unconstrained APIs.
notes_ci: Initial CI run had a flaky fuzz target failure; reran constrained fuzz job with updated seed corpus and all checks passed. Full test matrix: linux, mac, windows, dockerized runtime, integration streaming tests; performance benchmarks added as optional job.
